title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 340
paragraphs: This pyramid was built in the form of steps — what some call “rows” and others “bases.” After they had first made it this way, they raised the remaining stones using machines made of short pieces of timber. They lifted the stones first from the ground up to the first stage of the steps, and when a stone reached that stage, it was placed on another machine standing on the first step, and from there it was drawn up to the second stage by yet another machine. For there were as many machines as there were courses of steps — or perhaps they used one and the same machine, built to be easily carried, shifting it to each stage in turn so they could lift the stones up. Let it be told both ways, according to how it is reported. In any case, the highest parts of the pyramid were finished first, and afterwards they worked their way down, finishing the parts next to those, and last of all they finished the parts near the ground and the lowest courses. On the pyramid it is recorded in Egyptian writing how much was spent on radishes, onions, and leeks for the workmen; and if I correctly remember what the interpreter told me in reading this inscription, the sum came to one thousand six hundred talents of silver. If that is so, how much more must have been spent besides on the iron tools with which they worked, and on the bread and clothing for the workmen, considering that they were building these works for the length of time already mentioned, and were also occupied for no short period — I suppose — in cutting and transporting the stones and in excavating the underground chambers?
